# HTTP APIs

Both apps also serve interactive docs at `/docs` while running.

## Pipeline API (default http://localhost:8100)

### `GET /health`

Liveness: answers if the API process is up.

### `GET /config`

The reliability settings this deployment is running with (workers get the same environment).

### `POST /calls`

Start a call pipeline. Saves the call, then queues its ingest task; returns immediately with the call id (status PENDING). Optional `faults` inject a failure into a chunk, e.g. `{"2": "crash"}`.

JSON body: `title` (string); `num_chunks` (integer); `faults` (object)

### `GET /calls`

The most recent calls (newest first), without their chunks.

Parameters: `limit` (query)

### `GET /calls/{call_id}`

One call with every chunk: status, attempts, which worker ran it, progress and the last error.

Parameters: `call_id` (path, required)

### `GET /calls/{call_id}/events`

The audit trail: every claim, takeover, retry, skip and completion, in order.

Parameters: `call_id` (path, required)

### `GET /dead-letters`

Peek (without consuming) at messages parked in the dead_letter queue.

Parameters: `count` (query)

## Visualizer API (default http://localhost:8200)

### `GET /api/health`

Is the monitor up, is it connected to the broker, and how much has it seen? `dropped_events` counts events discarded because a run grew too large.

### `GET /api/states`

The state table (`states.json`) the UI renders: every task state, its stage, what it means and the settings that change it.

### `GET /api/runs`

Summaries of the most recent runs, newest first. A run is a root task and everything it spawned.

Parameters: `limit` (query)

### `GET /api/runs/{run_id}`

One run in full: its tasks (each with a timeline) and the edges between them, including inferred join edges. 404 if the run was evicted from the bounded store.

Parameters: `run_id` (path, required)

### `GET /api/workers`

Workers seen, with status `online`, `offline` (announced shutdown) or `lost` (silent for too long), and their own heartbeat period.

### `GET /api/queues`

Measured ready/unacked per queue, from RabbitMQ's Prometheus plugin (RabbitMQ only, optional).

### `GET /api/config`

Global settings in effect on live workers (only those the state table references).

### `GET /api/catalog`

The demo scenarios that can be launched, or `enabled: false` when the monitor runs read-only.

### `POST /api/launch`

Start a named demo scenario. Only available when the monitor was started with `--catalog`; unknown scenarios are 404 and invalid parameters 422. There is no way to send an arbitrary task.

JSON body: `scenario` (string, required); `params` (object)

### `GET /api/stream`

Server-Sent Events: one `snapshot` event, then `run` (full view of any run that changed) and `workers` events.
